newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sets new rules for mining companies.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sets new rules for mining companies.

text.p: The Philippines government said on Thursday that mining companies operating in the country have to pay one percent of output as royalty to indigenous tribes whose ancestral lands were being mined.

The new implementing guideline also require mining companies to contribute at least one percent of their mining and milling costs every year to community development projects, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources said in a statement.

The department issued the new set of rules to the Philippine Mining Act 1995 after an accidental waste spillage from a mine tailings dam leaked into nearby rivers in central Philippines earlier this year.
"The amendments to the IRR (implementing rules and regulations) were designed to strengthen our mining laws in pursuance of our thrust of environment protection," the department said.

The rules also require mining companies to obtain prior consent from indigenous peoples before exploration and set up post-operational land management plans for pits, waste dams, and tailings structures.
Industry leaders have projected at least $3 billion worth of new investments from Australia, Canada, United States and Germany to pour in due to the liberalisation of the industry.
